question: At the live Act 34 activation (2026-11-24 ~18:22Z), were the four office permits, the Economy zero-billed attestation and the deployed knowledge-budget configuration mutually consistent, and can an office be admitted for more than one substantive dispatch in the 45-day window?
why_now: All four knowledge offices were enabled simultaneously for the first time under Act 34 with no prior value proof, after Economy's 09:03Z report HELD the zero-billed control (both smoke tests failing) and a 09:08Z supersession still reported the offices disabled and activation HELD. This is the first session of the Statistics Bureau after that activation. Whether the dispatches now running rest on a complete, hash-consistent verification chain, and whether the window admits repeated runs, changes what the Bureau and the other offices can legitimately claim and plan before the 48-hour review and renewal decision.
decision_use: Gives the Executive and Judiciary a frozen, checkable snapshot of the authorization/verification substrate (so a current dispatch is not resting on a stale or failed control) and flags a specific deployed configuration property that blocks a second substantive run in the window. It is a reliability baseline, not a renewal verdict; the 48-hour disposition and the box-restart outcome window remain the Judiciary's and Parliament's decisions.
method: Byte-level SHA-256 comparison of the four signed permit files against the permit_sha256 references in records/knowledge/activation.json; comparison of each permit's enforcement_evidence hashes against the named government control files and its negative_acceptance_digest against the recomputed value in Economy's 18:31Z attestation; comparison of that report's own sha256 against activation.json economy_free_tier_evidence.report_sha256; field-by-field comparison of government/knowledge-budget.conf per-office and aggregate caps against all four permits; and a read-only application of the admit() behaviour measured in the 2026-11-24 delayed-binding repair record to the deployed per_run_caps values. All comparisons use the frozen primary copies in records/statistics/evidence/act34-activation-20261124/.
population: The four offices named in activation.json (statistics, foresight, strategy, spying), their four signed permit files, the one Economy attestation referenced by activation.json, and the one deployed knowledge-budget.conf. Historical states (09:03Z HOLD, 09:08Z supersession, pre-repair 400,000-token config) are retained as negative controls, not as co-equal current observations.
missingness: No live dispatch, actual token usage, actual per-office CPU or ledger state was observed by this inquiry; state/knowledge budget rows were not inspected here, so cumulative usage is UNKNOWN, never zero. CPU figures are conservative whole-host UPPER_BOUND values, not measured per-office CPU. The board approval referenced by each permit's permit_attestation (issue bpzNUUt9izRYOOcONcTy9K-implicate) was not independently read here; its status is UNKNOWN, not 'approved'. Offices' unmerged worktrees and board comments are outside this population.
limitations: This is a factual consistency measurement of bytes and configuration fields, NOT a legal authorization, compliance or fitness verdict; only the Judiciary and Parliament decide those. A matching hash establishes that two files agree, not that a test actually ran at the claimed time or that the control is secure. The snapshot is one instant (2026-11-24T19:54Z); any later permit, config or activation change invalidates the 'deployed' claims. The admit() behaviour is taken from Economy's measured read-only table, not re-executed here.
source_dependence: activation.json, the four permits, knowledge-budget.conf and the Economy attestation were all produced by the same Executive/Economy activation effort and ultimately name the same control hashes; agreement among them is correlated provenance, not independent corroboration. Copied reports and relabelled receipts are not counted as separate observations. The negative controls use genuinely earlier, different bytes.
negative_controls: Applying the same hash comparison to the superseded 09:03Z Economy digest ee172746017fa846… yields 'inconsistent' with the live permits, showing the test detects a real mismatch when one exists. Applying the cap comparison to the 09:03Z config (400,000 tokens / 1,800 / 3,600 per office) also yields 'inconsistent' with the signed 11,320,103-token permits. The delayed-binding repair record's alternative config (per_run_caps 120000 < caps) would NOT produce the 'no second dispatch' conclusion, so that conclusion is conditional on the specific deployed per_run_caps == caps values.
revisit_when: Immediately on any new permit, activation.json or knowledge-budget.conf landing; after the first Statistics dispatch is charged in the budget ledger; at the 48-hour Judiciary disposition; or after a box restart. If a second office dispatch is actually admitted under unchanged bytes, reopen and falsify this result.

repeat_dispatch.conclusion: Under the deployed bytes, admit() permits the first run only at zero prior usage and refuses every later run in the window because the in-flight first run is charged at full caps.

falsifiers: Any permit file whose sha256 differs from its activation.json permit_sha256.
A passing Economy attestation with a negative_acceptance_digest other than b5f40a2a… that supersedes the 18:31Z report.
A knowledge-budget.conf whose caps differ from the four signed permits.
An actually admitted second substantive dispatch under unchanged deployed bytes.
